question_types_in_exam.summary: RBSE Class 12 Accountancy paper mein 23 questions hain. Q1 = 12 MCQ (12 marks). Q2 = 6 Fill blanks (6 marks). Q3 = 12 Very Short (1 mark each = 12 marks). Q4-Q16 = Short Answer (2 marks each = 26 marks). Q17-Q20 = Medium Answer (3 marks each = 12 marks). Q21-Q23 = Long Answer (4 marks each = 12 marks). Total = 80 marks.

key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Normal Profit = Capital x Normal Rate of Return / 100; Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit; Goodwill = Super Profit x Years of Purchase
key_calculations_to_practice.example: Capital=4,00,000, Normal Rate=10%, Average Profit=60,000 → Normal Profit=40,000; Super Profit=20,000; Goodwill=20,000x3=60,000

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Interest on Drawing — Beginning of Month
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Interest = Total Drawing x Rate/100 x 6.5/12
key_calculations_to_practice.note: Beginning of each month = 6.5 months average period

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Interest on Drawing — End of Month
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Interest = Total Drawing x Rate/100 x 5.5/12
key_calculations_to_practice.note: End of each month = 5.5 months average period

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Interest on Drawing — Beginning of Quarter
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Interest = Total Drawing x Rate/100 x 7.5/12
key_calculations_to_practice.note: Beginning of each quarter = 7.5 months average period (MCQ repeat)

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: New Profit Sharing Ratio on Admission
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Old partners sacrifice their share; New Partner's share given; Remaining share = 1 - New Partner's share; Old partners get remaining in old ratio
Sacrificing Ratio = Old Ratio - New Ratio
Gaining Ratio = New Ratio - Old Ratio (on retirement/death)
Total capital of firm = Partner's capital / (1 - new partner's share); Goodwill = Total capital - Actual capital of all partners

key_calculations_to_practice.example: ₹4 per share on 1500 shares, 2 months = 6000 x 12% x 2/12 = 120

key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Revenue from Operations / Average Inventory; Average Inventory = COGS / Turnover Ratio

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Current Ratio + Liquidity Ratio — Inventory Calculation
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Current Assets = Current Ratio x Current Liabilities; Liquid Assets = Liquidity Ratio x Current Liabilities; Inventory = Current Assets - Liquid Assets
COGS = Opening Stock + Net Purchases + Direct Expenses - Closing Stock
Premium = Face Value of Debentures x Premium %
key_calculations_to_practice.example: 5,00,000 issued at par, redeemable at 10% premium → Premium = 50,000

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Gain on Cancellation of Own Debentures
key_calculations_to_practice.example: Face Value=4,00,000, Purchase Price=92 per debenture (4000 debentures) → Purchase=3,68,000; Gain=32,000

key_calculations_to_practice.topic: Number of Debentures Issued at Discount
key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Number = Amount to be paid / Issue Price per debenture
key_calculations_to_practice.example: Machine=2,00,000, paid ₹2,000 by cheque, remaining=1,98,000; Issue at 10% discount on ₹100 = ₹90; Debentures = 1,98,000/90 = 2200

key_calculations_to_practice.formula: Start with Net Profit; Add back non-cash items (Depreciation, Transfer to Reserve); Adjust working capital changes (Stock, Debtors, Creditors); Deduct tax paid
